result.question: Prehistoric rock paintings of India offer a window into the life of early humans. Discuss with reference to Bhimbetka and other sites. (Answer in 150 words)

directives.meaning: Look at the issue from more than one side, with reasons, and reach a balanced view.

sentences.text: India's earliest paintings, dating from the Upper Palaeolithic, survive on the walls and ceilings of rock shelters.
The first discovery of rock paintings in India was made in 1867-68 by Archibald Carlleyle, before the find at Altamira in Spain.
The largest and most spectacular rock-shelter complex is Bhimbetka in the Vindhya hills of Madhya Pradesh, discovered in 1957-58 by Vishnu Shridhar Wakankar.
Upper Palaeolithic paintings are linear figures of huge animals such as bison, elephants and rhinos, in green and dark red.
The Mesolithic phase has the largest number of paintings, smaller in size, in which hunting scenes predominate alongside dances and honey collection.
Artists ground minerals into pigments, obtaining red from haematite (geru) and green from chalcedony, and mixed them with water, fat or resin.
At Lakhudiyar on the Suyal river in Uttarakhand, superimposed layers run from black to red ochre to white and include hand-linked dancers.
These paintings reveal early beliefs and daily life, and their fragile sites need protection from vandalism and weathering.
